newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian aid may move before U.N. security ready.
newsitem.headline: Albanian aid may move before U.N. security ready.

text.p: The first shipment of emergency food aid to Albania will be distributed to isolated villages even if multinational security forces are not yet in place to protect the convoys, a U.N. relief official said on Sunday.

A first boat carrying 400 tonnes of flour and beans will arrive in the western Albanian port of Durres on Tuesday, and a United Nations World Food Programme spokeswoman in Tirana said the aid will be immediately relayed.
"Obviously we would prefer a security escort, but we cannot wait to go ahead and distribute the food supplies," said spokeswoman Laura Boldrini.
A Italian-led multinational security force of 6,000 soldiers has begun arriving in Albania but the bulk of troops on the U.N.-backed mission are not expected until Tuesday.
Nearly 300 people have been killed and 700 wounded during weeks of armed anarchy that erupted after the collapse of popular get-rich-quick investment schemes.

"The Italians are not sure if they will be ready to escort us on Tuesday," Boldrini told Reuters. "They need a few days to settle down. We cannot keep the commodities waiting in the port. They might be looted. We have to go ahead. People are in need."
Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi told a news conference in Tirana on Sunday: "If we bring the aid but don't protect the warehouses, there is no point in bringing the aid."

Boldrini said with or without the security escorts, four trucks carrying 100 tonnes of food supplies will travel on Tuesday to the central town of Elbasan, about 100 km (60 miles) southeast of Durres.
Another 10 trucks carrying 200 tonnes will be sent to the isolated mountain village of Kukes, 250 km (150 miles) to the north, on Wednesday.
There are no immediate plans to send trucks to the south, controlled by armed rebels. But relief workers will carry smaller amounts of food supplies in ordinary cars to several southern towns.
The wheat flour and beans will be distributed to destitute families, orphanages and centres for elderly and handicapped.
Although there is food in markets, Boldrini said people often cannot afford it and the institutions caring for them have been left without means in the collapsing state.
While there are no reports of starvation or famine, she said hunger was becoming a problem in remote areas of the impoverished nation.
"We are here to cope with an emergency," she added. "We have to go ahead. There are very needy people there and we cannot wait any longer."
Local leaders had pledged to organise protection for the convoys, she said. Army arsenals were looted after soldiers abandoned their posts and banditry has been rampant ever since.

The security force that began arriving on Friday will focus on food and medicine supplies. Troops from Italy, France, Spain, Turkey, Romania, Greece, Austria and Denmark will guard harbours and Tirana airport.
"This is just the first delivery," Boldrini added. "If we can work out the distribution system we will expand it to the whole country. We hope to implement this very soon."
